mainTopic: Checking family lineage (יוחסין) before marrying into כהונה: how far to check, the presumption of fitness, and which ancestors' roles prove clean lineage
overview: This amud finishes explaining how many generations of mothers must be checked, reading the משנה's 'one more' as 'one more pair.' רב says the משנה's checking follows רבי מאיר, while the חכמים hold that families are presumed fit; two versions of רב's words are given, and in the second one checking is needed once someone raises an ערער. The גמרא then explains the משנה's list of ancestors who make further checking unnecessary. These are a כהן at the מזבח, a לוי on the דוכן, and a member of the סנהדרין, whose members had to be free of any 'blemish'; the verses show this means lineage, not only bodily defects. Public officers prove lineage only in ירושלים, and charity collectors prove it because their quarrels would expose any flaw. A story with רב יוסף teaches that public posts go only to someone 'from among your brothers,' which includes one whose mother was born Jewish. Places differed on appointing converts. Finally, signers in ציפורי and soldiers of בית דוד prove lineage, and the גמרא answers challenges from warriors who seem to have been converts and from דוד's four hundred youths.

steps.title: Reading the statement as speaking about a Levite or Israelite woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: רב אדא בר אהבה's statement is read as speaking about a לויה or a בת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sets it up as speaking about a Levite woman or an Israelite woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started on the previous page. It says the earlier statement is talking about a לויה or a בת ישראל, not a כהנת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires one extra generation of checking for a לויה or ישראלית compared to a כהנת. By applying the statement to them, the extra checking fits the משנה, so there is no clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets it up as / reads it as speaking about
A woman from a family of לויים
An Israelite woman, not from a כהן or לוי family

phrases.english: He sets it up as referring to a Levite woman or an Israelite woman.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the earlier אמורא from the previous page. His ruling is now read as matching the משנה's case of one more generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a defense that began before this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement seemed to clash with the משנה's count of generations.
steps.terutzMaskana: It speaks about a לויה or a בת ישראל, who need one more generation of checking.

steps.title: Does the ברייתא argue with the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The ruling now fits the משנה, but it seems to clash with a ברייתא's count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then shall we say the ברייתא disagrees with the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. The fix made the ruling fit the משנה, but now the ברייתא seems to give a different number of generations than the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says 'one more' for a לויה or ישראלית. The ברייתא's count seems to add more than that. The גמרא does not want to say that a ברייתא and the משנה argue.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: But shall we say the ברייתא disagrees?
phrases.notes: מַתְנִיתָא here means a ברייתא, not our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of the previous answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the משנה's count fits with the ברייתא's count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה adds only one generation, the ברייתא's larger count would mean the two sources argue.

steps.title: 'One more' means one more pair
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's 'one more' means one pair, so it agrees with the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'one more' mean? One pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no argument. When the משנה says 'one more,' it means one more pair of mothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The checking goes back on both the mother's side and the father's side. So 'one more' adds one generation on each side, which is two mothers. Read this way, the משנה and the ברייתא give the same total.
steps.whatToRemember: For a לויה or ישראלית, the משנה's 'one more' means one more pair, one mother on each side. So the משנה and the ברייתא agree.

phrases.english: No, what is 'one more'?
One pair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading the משנה's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One more' meant a single additional mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One more' means a pair, one on each side, matching the ברייתא.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי מאיר; the חכמים presume families are fit
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the משנה's checking rule is רבי מאיר's view, while the חכמים say all families are presumed fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי מאיר. But the חכמים say all families keep a presumption of being fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב says the whole checking requirement in the משנה is only רבי מאיר's opinion. The חכמים say there is no need to check, because families are presumed fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This changes the picture of the משנה. It is not a rule everyone agrees to. Under the חכמים, a family is assumed to be fit unless something shows otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the opinion of רבי מאיר
In a presumed status of being fit

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of a חזקה of fitness for families is central to how יוחסין is handled in practice.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: 'This' means our משנה's rule about checking the mothers.

phrases.english: but the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִשְׁפָּחוֹת בְּחֶזְקַת כְּשֵׁרוֹת הֵן עוֹמְדוֹת.
phrases.english: All families stand in a presumption of fitness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about who holds the משנה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים hold that all families are presumed fit.

steps.title: רב said elsewhere the משנה is only when someone objected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: didn't רב, through רב חמא בר גוריא, say the משנה speaks only when an objection was raised?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: Our משנה is when someone raises an objection about him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רב really said this. Another report from רב says the משנה is only about a family that someone has challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה deals only with a family that was challenged, then everyone could agree with it. A family with no challenge would be presumed fit by all. That conflicts with calling the משנה only רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An objection or challenge to someone's lineage

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Hama bar Gurya say in the name of Rav:
Our Mishnah is when one raises an objection about him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's report of רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's report that רב made the משנה רבי מאיר's view only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another report has רב limiting the משנה to a challenged family. That reading makes it agreed by all, which contradicts the first report.

steps.title: Two different traditions of רב
steps.stepSummary: The two statements come from different students reporting רב differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever taught this one did not teach that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reports are two different traditions of what רב said. One student did not report the other's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to fit both statements together. It accepts that רב יהודה and רב חמא בר גוריא quoted רב differently, so there is no contradiction within one tradition.

keyTerms.term: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָא לָא מַתְנֵי הָא
keyTerms.meaning: The one who taught this did not teach that; these are two separate traditions

phrases.english: The one who teaches this —
does not teach that.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָא לָא מַתְנֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by splitting the reports.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements were one teacher's view and contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are different reports of רב, so they do not contradict.

steps.title: Another version: both statements of רב fit together
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב חמא בר גוריא's statement adds to רב יהודה's: when an objection is raised, one must check.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is רבי מאיר's view, but the חכמים say all families are presumed fit. רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: If someone raises an objection, one must check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the whole discussion. Here the two statements of רב do not clash. They work together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב חמא בר גוריא is not explaining the משנה. He is adding that even for the חכמים, a challenged family must be checked. So the חזקה of fitness holds only until an objection is raised.
steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, families are presumed fit, but once someone raises an ערער, checking is required.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. In the first, רב חמא בר גוריא explains the משנה, and the two reports clash. In the second, he gives an extra rule that fits with רב יהודה.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
but the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת בְּחֶזְקַת כְּשֵׁרוֹת הֵן עוֹמְדוֹת.
phrases.english: All families stand in a presumption of fitness.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Hama bar Gurya said in the name of Rav:
If one raises an objection about him,
he must check after her.
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the woman he wants to marry. He has to look into her family line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version that avoids the contradiction completely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Families are presumed fit, but once an objection is raised, one must check.

steps.title: Why no checking past the altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: no checking is needed past an ancestor who served at the מזבח. It asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One does not check from the altar and up.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. If a woman's ancestor served as a כהן at the מזבח, no one checks further back. The גמרא asks for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives this exemption without explaining it. The גמרא wants to know why serving at the מזבח counts as proof of a clean family line.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar in the בית המקדש
And upward (further back in the generations)

phrases.english: One does not check from the altar and upward.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. Once you reach an ancestor who served at the מזבח, you stop checking.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בּוֹדְקִין מִן הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּלְמַעְלָה. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason serving at the מזבח ends the need to check.

steps.title: He was already checked before serving
steps.stepSummary: No כהן was allowed to serve at the מזבח without his lineage being checked first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had not checked him, they would not have let him go up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a כהן serving at the מזבח had already been checked. Otherwise he would never have been allowed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The service itself shows that a check was already done. So the families above that ancestor were already examined, and checking again is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: They would bring up (let him go up)

phrases.english: If they had not checked him,
they would not have brought him up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּבַדְקוּהּ לָא הֲווֹ מַסְּקִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Service at the מזבח shows his lineage had already been checked.

steps.title: Why no checking past the platform?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: no checking past an ancestor who stood on the דוכן. It asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not from the platform and up.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next exemption in the משנה. This is a לוי ancestor who stood on the דוכן to sing in the מקדש. The גמרא asks for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parallels the מזבח case, but for לויים. The question is what shows that a לוי on the דוכן had been checked.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform where the לויים sang in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And not from the platform and upward.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא מִן הַדּוּכָן וּלְמַעְלָה. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question on the next clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why standing on the דוכן ends the need to check.

steps.title: Lineage experts sat there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching: experts in the lineage of כהנים and לויים sat there.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: For there sat those who verify the lineage of the כהונה and the lineage of the לויים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a known teaching. The people who checked the family lines of כהנים and לויים sat there, so anyone who served was checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the lineage checkers were right there, no לוי reached the דוכן without being examined. So, like the מזבח, serving on the דוכן proves the family above him was already checked.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (quoting a known teaching)
Those who verify the lineage of כהנים
Those who verify the lineage of לויים

steps.whatToRemember: Serving at the מזבח or on the דוכן proves the family line was already checked, so further checking is not needed.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
For there would sit
phrases.notes: 'There' is the place in the מקדש where the experts sat.

phrases.english: those who verify the lineage of the priesthood and those who verify the lineage of the Levites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by quoting a teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lineage checkers sat there, so whoever served on the דוכן had already been checked.

steps.title: Why no checking past a member of the סנהדרין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה, an ancestor who sat on the סנהדרין, and asks why no further checking is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: no checking is needed past an ancestor who sat on the סנהדרין. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה's list, the סנהדרין, and asks for the reason behind it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the מזבח and דוכן questions in steps 8 and 10. The גמרא wants to know what guarantees that a member of the סנהדרין had clean lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: And above, meaning further back in the family line

phrases.english: Nor from the Sanhedrin and above.
phrases.notes: This is the next line of the משנה. Once you find an ancestor who sat on the סנהדרין, you don't need to check further back.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of reason questions on the משנה's list of ancestors
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an ancestor on the סנהדרין makes further lineage checks unnecessary

steps.title: The court was clean of any blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף taught that the court was clean both in justice and of any blemish, meaning flawed lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: just as the court is clean in justice, so it is clean of every blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a teaching of רב יוסף: the court had no one with a 'blemish' on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'blemish' means a flaw in family lineage. If only people with clean lineage could sit on the court, then a member of the סנהדרין is proof that the family is clean.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (a teaching from the time of the משנה)

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef taught:
Just as the court is clean in justice,
so too it is clean of any blemish.
phrases.notes: Here 'blemish' means a flaw in family lineage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The court had to be free of any blemish, including flawed lineage

steps.title: The verse: no blemish in you
steps.stepSummary: מרימר gives the verse behind רב יוסף's teaching: 'You are all fair, my love, and there is no blemish in you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר said: Which verse teaches this? 'You are all fair, my love, and there is no blemish in you.'
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר gives a verse as the source for רב יוסף's rule that the court has no blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse from שיר השירים is read as praise of the leaders of the nation, the court. It says they have 'no blemish', and the next steps will ask what kind of blemish that means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (the source in תנ״ך)

phrases.english: Mareimar said:
What is the verse?
"You are all fair, my love,
and there is no blemish in you."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 4:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a verse to support רב יוסף's teaching
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the court was free of any blemish

steps.title: Maybe the verse means a physical blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe 'blemish' in the verse means a real bodily defect, not flawed lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it means an actual blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading of the verse. Maybe it only means judges can't have a physical defect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse is about bodily defects, it says nothing about lineage. Then there would be no proof that a member of the סנהדרין had clean lineage.

phrases.english: Say it means an actual blemish!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 14 reads the verse
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'blemish' in שיר השירים as flawed lineage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of מום is a physical defect, so the verse may not be about lineage at all

steps.title: Physical blemishes come from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the rule against physical defects is learned from 'with you', meaning 'like you', so the שיר השירים verse is free to teach lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The verse says, 'That they may stand there with you.' 'With you' means people like you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that we already know about physical blemishes from another verse about the elders of משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With you' means the elders had to be like משה, whole in body. Since bodily defects are already covered by that verse, the verse 'no blemish in you' must be teaching something new: clean lineage.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
The verse says:
"That they may stand there with you,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 11:16

phrases.english: "With you" means like you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separate source for the physical rule frees the first verse for lineage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שיר השירים verse is about physical defects
steps.terutzMaskana: Physical defects are learned from 'with you'; the שיר השירים verse teaches clean lineage

steps.title: Maybe that was because of the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the elders of משה had to be whole only because the שכינה rested on them, not because they were judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it was because of the שכינה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אחא בר יעקב's proof. Maybe 'like you' was a special rule for elders who received prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule came from the שכינה resting on them, it would not apply to ordinary judges. Then we would still need the שיר השירים verse for physical defects, and the proof for lineage falls away.

phrases.english: But perhaps it was because of the Shechinah?
phrases.notes: Those elders were receiving prophecy from ה׳, so maybe that is the only reason they had to be like משה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from במדבר 11:16 for ordinary judges
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse may be a special requirement because of the שכינה, not a rule for all judges

steps.title: A verse about ordinary judges also says 'with you'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a verse about appointing ordinary judges that also says 'with you', meaning 'like you'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The verse says, 'So it will be easier for you, and they will carry the load with you.' That means people like you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a different verse, about ordinary judges, which also says 'with you'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No שכינה is mentioned in this verse, so 'like you' must apply to all judges: they must be whole in body. So physical defects are covered, and the שיר השירים verse again teaches clean lineage.
steps.whatToRemember: A member of the סנהדרין proves clean lineage, because the court had to be free of any 'blemish' (שיר השירים 4:7). Physical defects are learned from a separate verse, 'with you', meaning 'like you'.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said,
the verse says:
"So shall it be easier for you
and they shall carry the load with you,"
phrases.notes: שמות 18:22

phrases.english: meaning like you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 17 with a new verse
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source free of the שכינה objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like you' may apply only to those on whom the שכינה rested
steps.terutzMaskana: All judges must be whole in body, so the שיר השירים verse teaches lineage

steps.title: Are people of flawed lineage never appointed to public posts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about ancestors who were public officers and asks: does this mean we never appoint people with flawed lineage?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: anyone whose ancestors were known as public officers. Does that mean we don't appoint people with flawed lineage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and draws a conclusion from it. This sets up a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being a public officer proves clean lineage, it seems people with flawed lineage were never given public posts. The גמרא is about to test that idea against another teaching.

phrases.english: Anyone whose ancestors were established
as public officers.
Is this to say that we do not appoint people of flawed lineage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה implies that people with flawed lineage are never appointed to public posts

steps.title: But a ממזר may judge money cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts this with a teaching that 'all' may judge money cases, which רב יהודה said includes a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Contrast it with this: All are fit to judge money cases, but not all are fit to judge capital cases. We asked: what does 'all' include? רב יהודה said: it includes a ממזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 19. It brings a teaching showing that even a ממזר can be a judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a ממזר can judge money cases, then people with flawed lineage can hold public positions. So how can the משנה treat a public officer as proof of clean lineage?

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast them (two sources that seem to clash)
A child from a forbidden union, who has flawed lineage

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of cases. A ממזר may judge only money cases, not capital cases. The question is only that he can hold any judging position at all.

phrases.english: And contrast it with this:
All are fit to judge money cases,
but not all are fit
to judge capital cases.
And we discussed it:
"All" comes to include what?
And Rav Yehuda said:
To include a mamzer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the conclusion drawn in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that public appointees always have clean lineage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ממזר may serve as a judge in money cases, so holding a public post does not prove clean lineage

steps.title: אביי: the משנה speaks about ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה refers to public officers in Jerusalem, where only people with clean lineage were appointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The משנה is talking about Jerusalem.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by limiting the משנה to officers in Jerusalem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general a ממזר may judge money cases. But in Jerusalem they were strict and appointed only people with clean lineage, so an officer there does prove clean lineage.

phrases.english: Abaye said: In Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's case of public officers is about Jerusalem, where only people with clean lineage were appointed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a specific place
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means any public officer anywhere
steps.terutzMaskana: Only public officers in Jerusalem prove clean lineage; elsewhere a ממזר may judge money cases

steps.title: A teaching from the school of Levi agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעון בר זירא taught the same thing in the קידושין teachings of the school of לוי: 'in ירושלים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שמעון בר זירא taught the same in the Kiddushin of the school of לוי: In Jerusalem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for אביי's answer from an older teaching that also says 'in Jerusalem'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's limit is not just his own idea. A teaching from the school of לוי says the same, so the answer is backed up.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught (support from a teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: An ancestor who was a public officer proves clean lineage only for officers in Jerusalem, where they were strict. Elsewhere, even a ממזר could judge money cases.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַב שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר זֵירָא
phrases.english: And so Rav Shimon bar Zeira taught
in the Kiddushin teachings of the school of Levi:
In Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן תָּנֵי רַב שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in step 21
steps.raayaObject: אביי's limit of the משנה to Jerusalem
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Kiddushin teaching of the school of לוי, taught by רב שמעון בר זירא

steps.title: Why do charity collectors' families need no check?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about גבאי צדקה and asks for the reason behind it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if your ancestors were charity collectors, you may marry into כהונה without a lineage check. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the משנה's list, charity collectors, and asks why it works. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier items, like judges, made sense because people were checked before being appointed. A charity collector is not obviously checked, so the גמרא wants to know why his family counts as proven clean.

keyTerms.meaning: Charity collectors appointed by the community
May marry off their children (here, into כהונה) without a check

phrases.english: And charity collectors may marry [into the כהונה].
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה: a family with charity collectors among its ancestors may marry into כהונה without being checked.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the public-officers line to the next item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why being a charity collector proves that one's family is clean.

steps.title: Collectors fight with people, so any flaw would be exposed
steps.stepSummary: Charity collectors argue with people, even taking collateral on ערב שבת. If their family had a flaw, someone would have shouted it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they argue with people. As the Master said: we take collateral for charity even on Friday afternoon. So if there were a flaw in the collector's family, it would become publicly known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: charity collectors make enemies, so their family background gets loudly exposed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof does not come from a formal check. It comes from conflict. Collectors grab collateral even when people are rushed and tense before שבת. Angry people would shout out any family flaw, so silence shows the family is clean.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the busy time right before שבת
Literally 'a voice': public talk, a rumor

phrases.english: Since they quarrel with people,
as the Master said:
We take collateral for charity
even on the eve of שבת,
and if it were so that there is [a flaw],
it would have publicity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Collectors quarrel with people, so any lineage flaw would have been publicized. No rumor means the family is clean.
steps.whatToRemember: A charity collector's family is proven clean because his enemies would have exposed any flaw.

steps.title: Two men compete for a city post
steps.stepSummary: The host of רב אדא בר אהבה was a convert, and he and רב ביבי argued over who would lead the city. They brought the case to רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה's host was a convert. He and רב ביבי were arguing. Each one said: I will run the city's affairs. They came before רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a convert's family and public office. This sets up רב יוסף's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the topic of who may be appointed to public positions. The new question is whether someone with a convert in his background may hold a city post.

keyTerms.meaning: His host (the man he stayed with)
Leadership or official service of the city

phrases.english: The host of רב אדא בר אהבה
was a convert,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה קָא מִנְּצֵי אִיהוּ וְרַב בִּיבִי,
phrases.english: and he and רב ביבי were quarreling.

phrases.aramaic: מָר אָמַר: אֲנָא עָבֵידְנָא סְרָרוּתָא דְמָתָא,
phrases.english: One said: I will perform the leadership of the city,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר אָמַר: אֲנָא עָבֵידְנָא סְרָרוּתָא דְמָתָא.
phrases.english: and the other said: I will perform the leadership of the city.
They came before רב יוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוּשְׁפִּיזְכָּנֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה גִּיּוֹרָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from lineage proofs to a story about a convert's family holding public office.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a convert's family member and רב ביבי both want the city post.

steps.title: Only someone 'from among your brothers' may be appointed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes the פסוק about appointing a king. The doubled verb teaches that every appointment must be of someone 'from among your brothers'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We learned: 'You shall surely set a king over you… from among your brothers.' Every appointment you make must be only from among your brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rules that a convert may not hold any public appointment, not just the position of king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק doubles the verb, 'שום תשים'. רב יוסף reads the extra word as stretching the rule from a king to every position of authority. At this point, the host seems to be ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall surely set': a doubled verb, read as including all appointments

phrases.english: He said to them: We learned:
"You shall surely set a king over you… from among your brothers",
phrases.notes: דברים 17:15

phrases.english: all appointments that you appoint
may be only from among your brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף gives a ruling on the dispute in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All positions of authority must go to someone 'from among your brothers', so a convert is not appointed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that a convert may not hold any public office, not only the office of king.

steps.title: What if his mother was born Jewish?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks whether the rule applies even when the person's mother is Jewish from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to him: Even if his mother is from Israel?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא speaks up for his host. He asks if the rule still applies when only the father was a convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא narrows the case. His host is not a convert himself. His father converted, but his mother was born Jewish. Does that still count as not 'from among your brothers'?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: רב אדא בר אהבה said to him:
Even if his mother is from Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: וַאֲפִילּוּ אִמּוֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the limits of רב יוסף's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether someone with a Jewish-born mother counts as 'from among your brothers'.

steps.title: A Jewish mother is enough, so the jobs are divided
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that a Jewish-born mother makes him 'from among your brothers'. רב ביבי, the great scholar, takes religious matters, and the host takes city matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If his mother is from Israel, 'from among your brothers' applies to him. Therefore, רב ביבי, who is a great man, should handle matters of Heaven, and the Master [the host] should handle the matters of the city.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rules that the host qualifies, and splits the leadership between the two men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only excludes someone with no Jewish-born parent. Since both men now qualify, רב יוסף does not pick one. He gives each a role that suits him.

keyTerms.meaning: I read [the פסוק] as applying to him
Matters of Heaven: communal religious affairs
Matters of the city: civic affairs

phrases.english: He said to him: [If] his mother is from Israel,
I read "from among your brothers" about him.

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכָּךְ רַב בִּיבִי דְּגַבְרָא רַבָּא הוּא –
phrases.english: Therefore, רב ביבי, who is a great man,
should oversee matters of Heaven,
and the Master should oversee matters of the city.
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the host, רב אדא's landlord.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִמּוֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מִקֶּרֶב אַחֶיךָ קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא's question and settles the dispute from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person whose mother is born Jewish counts as 'from among your brothers' and may be appointed.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on appointing converts does not apply to someone whose mother was born Jewish.

steps.title: אביי: host a scholar who will speak up for you
steps.stepSummary: אביי draws a lesson from the story: if you host a Torah scholar, pick one like רב אדא בר אהבה, who argues in his host's favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, whoever hosts a young Torah scholar should host one like רב אדא בר אהבה, who turns things around in his favor.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes the story with a practical life lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא's sharp question is what won his host the post. אביי praises a guest who uses his learning to protect the person who hosts him.

keyTerms.meaning: Turns things around in his favor

phrases.english: אביי said: Therefore,
one who lodges a young Torah scholar as his guest
should lodge one like רב אדא בר אהבה,
who turns things around for him in his favor.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets ('who knows how to turn'); the corrected wording in square brackets just says 'who turns'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a moral from the story just told.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Choose a scholar guest who will speak up for his host.

steps.title: Some אמוראים appointed converts
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבה בר אבוה would deal with converts and appoint them to positions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא would deal with them. רבה בר אבוה would deal with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that some sages were lenient and would place converts in positions of authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows a practice that seems more lenient than רב יוסף's broad reading. These sages were willing to give converts some public roles. The next step shows the opposite practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Deals with them (here, assigning converts to positions)

phrases.english: רבי זירא would deal with them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means converts. He would give them public positions.

phrases.english: רבה בר אבוה would deal with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a lenient practice regarding converts in public roles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא and רבה בר אבוה appointed converts to positions.

steps.title: Stricter places refused even minor posts to converts
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they would not appoint a convert even as an overseer of measures. In נהרדעא, not even as an overseer of irrigation.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West, they would not appoint even a supervisor of measures from them. In נהרדעא, they would not appoint even a supervisor of irrigation from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא contrasts the lenient practice with stricter places that kept converts out of even small jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These places applied 'all appointments' to its fullest. Even the smallest official role, like checking measures or managing water channels, counts as an appointment, so a convert could not hold it.

keyTerms.meaning: Overseer of measures (כור is a measure)

phrases.english: In the West, even an overseer of measures
they would not appoint from them.
In נהרדעא, even an overseer of irrigation
they would not appoint from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא אֲפִילּוּ רֵישׁ כּוֹרֵי לָא מוֹקְמִי מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the strict practice, in contrast to step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל and נהרדעא, converts were kept out of even the smallest public posts.
steps.whatToRemember: Places differed: some sages appointed converts, while ארץ ישראל and נהרדעא refused them even minor posts.

steps.title: Why does signing in ציפורי prove lineage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי from the משנה and asks for the reason behind his rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: even someone who was (a signer in the old court of ציפורי, his family does not need checking). What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, quotes רבי יוסי, and asks why his rule works. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says that a family whose ancestor signed as a witness in ציפורי does not need its lineage checked. The גמרא wants to know why a signature proves anything about family purity.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.' The rest of the quote from the משנה is assumed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even one who was, etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה line is about someone who signed as a witness in the old court of ציפורי.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the stories about converts to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a signature in ציפורי proves pure lineage.

steps.title: They checked before letting witnesses sign
steps.stepSummary: In ציפורי, witnesses were checked first and only then allowed to sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would check, and then have them sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the court in ציפורי checked every witness's lineage before letting him sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nobody could sign without being checked first, the signature itself shows the person was already examined and found to have good lineage. His descendants therefore don't need to be checked again.

phrases.english: They would examine, and then have them sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ציפורי court checked lineage before allowing anyone to sign, so the signature is proof of a check.

steps.title: The army list means דוד's troops
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the army list mentioned by רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס is the troops of בית דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס (says: even someone written in the king's army list, etc.). רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this means the troops of בית דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and tells us which army list it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says 'the king's army list'. שמואל makes it specific: the troops of בית דוד, who were all checked for pure lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: The House of David, the royal family

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה is about someone written in the king's army list.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
In the troops of the House of David.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The army list in the משנה refers to the soldiers of בית דוד.

steps.title: The verse behind the army rule
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives the פסוק showing that soldiers were listed by lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the verse? 'Reckoned by lineage, in the army, for war.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a פסוק that supports שמואל's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links 'lineage' (התיחשם) directly with army service. This shows that soldiers were registered by family background, so being on the list proves good lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse (that teaches this)?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
What is the verse?
"Reckoned by lineage for service in war."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 7:40

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for step 34.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's statement that David's soldiers were of checked lineage.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in דברי הימים א that ties lineage to army service.

steps.title: Why must soldiers have pure lineage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why soldiers needed pure lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it mattered that soldiers come from good families. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know that soldiers were checked, but not why lineage would matter on the battlefield.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in steps 34-35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the soldiers had to be of pure lineage.

steps.title: Their ancestors' merit protects them
steps.stepSummary: רב says soldiers had pure lineage so that their own merit and their ancestors' merit would help them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: so that their merit, and the merit of their ancestors, would help them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that pure lineage gives soldiers the extra protection of their fathers' merit in battle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is spiritual, not military. Soldiers from good families bring their ancestors' merit with them, and that merit helps them win.
steps.whatToRemember: David's soldiers were checked for lineage (שמואל), based on a פסוק (רב יוסף), so their ancestors' merit would help them (רב).

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
So that their merit
and the merit of their ancestors will help them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא זְכוּתָן וּזְכוּת אֲבוֹתָם מְסַיַּיעְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: So that their own merit and their ancestors' merit help them in war.

steps.title: Challenge from צלק העמוני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule: one of David's warriors was called צלק העמוני, which sounds like a convert from עמון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is צלק העמוני. Doesn't that mean he came from עמון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that all of David's soldiers had pure lineage. It points to a warrior whose title suggests he was a convert from עמון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'the Ammonite' means he was born in עמון and converted, then a convert served in David's army. That would mean the army list does not prove pure lineage.

phrases.english: But isn't there Zelek the Ammonite,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:37

phrases.english: what, is it not that he came from Ammon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that David's troops were all of pure lineage.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that David's soldiers were all of checked, pure lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A warrior called 'the Ammonite' seems to be a convert, which contradicts the claim of pure lineage.

steps.title: He only lived in עמון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that צלק just lived in עמון; he was born Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means he lived in עמון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule by explaining that 'the Ammonite' refers to where he lived, not where he came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The title describes his address, not his birth. A Jew living in עמון could be called 'the Ammonite', so the rule still stands.

phrases.english: No, it means that he lived in Ammon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The Ammonite' means a convert from עמון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The Ammonite' means a Jew who lived in עמון.

steps.title: Challenge from אוריה החתי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another warrior, אוריה החתי, who sounds like a convert from חת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is אוריה החתי. Doesn't that mean he came from חת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second warrior of David whose title suggests a non-Jewish origin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of attack as before: a title that seems to show the warrior was a convert.

keyTerms.meaning: Uriah the Hittite, one of David's warriors

phrases.english: But isn't there Uriah the Hittite,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:39

phrases.english: what, is it not that he came from Heth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge, parallel to step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that David's troops were all of pure lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'The Hittite' seems to show he was a convert from חת.

steps.title: He only lived in חת
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: אוריה only lived in חת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means he lived in חת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: the title refers to where he lived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'place of residence' answer also covers אוריה, so the rule about pure lineage survives this challenge too.

phrases.english: No, it means that he lived in Heth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 40.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The Hittite' means a convert from חת.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The Hittite' means a Jew who lived in חת.

steps.title: אתי הגתי must have been a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings אתי הגתי and blocks the 'he only lived there' answer: רב נחמן says אתי nullified an idol, and only a non-Jew can do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is אתי הגתי! And if you say he too just lived in גת, didn't רב נחמן say that אתי הגתי came and nullified it (the idol)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third warrior and closes the easy way out ahead of time. רב נחמן's statement shows that אתי was a non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, 'he lived there' solved every case. Here it fails, because אתי was able to nullify an idol (ביטול עבודה זרה), which only a non-Jew can do. So a man born a non-Jew seems to have been among David's soldiers. The גמרא gives no separate answer here. It adds another challenge with 'ועוד' in the next step, and the single answer in step 44 covers both.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say... (the גמרא predicts an answer and rejects it)
He nullified it (removed its status as an idol)
Ittai the Gittite, a soldier with David

steps.confusionAlert: The 'he only lived there' answer worked for צלק and אוריה, but it does not work here. The proof that אתי was a non-Jew comes from רב נחמן's statement, not from his title.

phrases.english: But isn't there Ittai the Gittite!
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 15:19

phrases.english: And if you would say, so too
that he lived in Gath,
but didn't Rav Naḥman say:
Ittai the Gittite came and nullified it!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the crown of the idol of עמון that David used. Only a non-Jew can nullify an idol, so אתי must have been one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, stronger challenge that rules out the answer used in steps 39 and 41 before it can be given.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that David's troops were all of pure lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן says אתי nullified an idol, which only a non-Jew can do. So 'he only lived in גת' cannot be the answer, and a convert served among David's men.

steps.title: דוד's four hundred youths, sons of captive women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule again. רב יהודה quotes רב that דוד had four hundred youths. They were all sons of a יפת תואר, wore non-Jewish hairstyles, and led the troops as the strongmen of דוד's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה also said in the name of רב: דוד had four hundred youths. All of them were sons of captive women. All of them had their hair cut in the קומי style or grew a בלורית. All of them sat in gold carriages and marched at the head of the troops. These were the strongmen of the house of דוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement of רב that seems to prove דוד's army included men without proper lineage. These were sons of captive non-Jewish women, and they were right at the front of the army.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 38-42 challenged the rule with single warriors who sounded like converts. This challenge is bigger: a whole group of four hundred, born to a יפת תואר, with non-Jewish hairstyles. They were not hidden in the back; they led the troops and were called the strongmen of דוד's house. So it seems people of flawed lineage were a central part of דוד's army.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman captured in war whom a Jewish soldier is allowed to marry (דברים 21:11). Her sons here are of flawed lineage.
A lock of hair grown long at the back of the head, a non-Jewish hairstyle.
Literally 'masters of fists': strongmen, tough fighters.

steps.confusionAlert: בני יפת תואר does not mean 'handsome sons.' It means sons of a יפת תואר, a captive woman from war. That is exactly why this is a challenge to their lineage.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And further, Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת יְלָדִים הָיוּ לוֹ לְדָוִד,
phrases.english: David had four hundred youths,
and all of them were sons of captive women,
and all of them had their hair cut in the komei style,
or they grew a belorit lock of hair,
phrases.notes: Both hairstyles are non-Jewish styles, another sign of where these youths came from.

phrases.english: and all of them sat in carriages of gold
and would march at the head of the troops,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן הֵן בַּעֲלֵי אֶגְרוֹפִים שֶׁל בֵּית דָּוִד!
phrases.english: and these very ones were the strongmen of the house of David!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the same series (Steps 38-42) against the rule that דוד's soldiers all had proper lineage. This one uses a whole group instead of a single warrior.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that everyone who went out in דוד's army had proper lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sons of a יפת תואר with non-Jewish hairstyles led דוד's troops and were his strongmen. So people of flawed lineage were in his army, and in a central role.

steps.title: They only marched to frighten the enemy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that these four hundred youths did not actually fight. They went out in front only to frighten everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went out only to frighten everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The four hundred youths were not real fighters in the army; their job was to march in front and scare people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about proper lineage applies to those who actually fought in דוד's wars. These youths were a show of strength: gold carriages and a frightening look at the front of the army. Since they did not do the fighting, they do not break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the world': everyone, people in general.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of proper lineage in דוד's army holds. Names like צלק העמוני and אוריה החתי, which sounded like converts, were explained as Jews who only lived in those places. אתי הגתי and the four hundred sons of a יפת תואר were not fighters; they only marched in front to frighten the enemy.

phrases.english: They would go only to frighten everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the combined challenge of Steps 42-43 (אתי הגתי and the four hundred youths) by redefining their role: they marched in front to frighten and did not fight.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the youths were not real soldiers, only a frightening display.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because they led the troops and were called strongmen, it seemed they were fighters in דוד's army.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only marched in front to frighten the enemy and did not fight. So the rule that the fighters had proper lineage still stands.
